stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep each slider — $q_1$, $q_2$, and $r$ — across at least half its range. Notice how doubling a charge doubles $F$, and how halving $r$ multiplies $F$ by four.
stages.concept: Coulomb's law: $F = k \cdot |q_1 q_2| / r^2$ with $k \approx 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N} \cdot \text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$. $F$ is linear in each charge and inverse-square in the separation $r$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target force $F^{*}$ is displayed. Adjust $q_1$, $q_2$, and $r$ until the live force arrow on $q_2$ matches the dashed target arrow.
stages.concept: Many $(q_1, q_2, r)$ triples yield the same $|F|$. The visualization couples all three parameters into a single scalar — use it to build intuition for the inverse-square scaling.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The force arrow is hidden. Only the target $F^{*}$ and the current slider values remain. Compute $q_1$, $q_2$, $r$ on paper so that $F = F^{*}$, then set the sliders and submit.
stages.concept: Inverse form: $r = \sqrt{k \cdot |q_1 q_2| / F^{*}}$, or equivalently $|q_1 q_2| = F^{*} r^{2} / k$. Fix two of the three variables at convenient values and solve for the third.

labels.tip1: sweep every slider at least half its range
labels.tip2: match the live arrow to the dashed target arrow
labels.tip3: compute q1, q2, r on paper — then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: F = k·|q1·q2|/r²  →  r = sqrt(k·|q1·q2|/F). Pick two charges, solve for r.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Anchor: 1 µC × 1 µC at r = 10 cm gives F = 0.9 N. Scale from there.

1.1: Nudge each slider. Which one changes the arrow the most?
1.2: Doubling q1 doubles F. Halving r multiplies F by four.
1.3: Coverage bars show your progress. Push each slider to both extremes.

2.1: The target |F*| is displayed. Rearrange F = k·|q1·q2|/r² to isolate one variable.
2.2: Fix q1 = q2 = 2 µC, then solve r = sqrt(k·|q1·q2|/F*).
2.3: Try r = sqrt(90·q1·q2/F*) with q, F in µC and N and r in cm. Any valid triple works.

3.1: The arrow is hidden, but the formula still holds. Write it on paper first.
3.2: In display units: F(N) = 90·q1(µC)·q2(µC)/r(cm)². Solve for one variable.
3.3: Pick round charges — e.g. q1 = q2 = 2 µC — then compute r = sqrt(90·q1·q2/F*).
